paper.title: Minimum mean-squared error estimation with bandit feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Adaptive estimation with bandit feedback (best m-subset identification under MSE objective, fixed confidence)
unmapped: Observations are i.i.d. zero-mean jointly Gaussian K-vectors with unknown covariance; the whole K-vector is observed each round
Objective: identify the m-subset minimizing the MSE psi(A)=Tr(Sigma_{A'A'} - Sigma_{A'A} Sigma_{AA}^{-1} Sigma_{AA'}) (correlation-based, not mean-based)
Variances satisfy 0 < l <= sigma_i^2 <= 1 (Assumption 1); eigenvalue bounds on Sigma_AA (Assumption 2)
settings.definition_quote: For all t=1,2,..., repeat: Observe a sample K-vector from the underlying multivariate Gaussian distribution. Choose to continue, or stop and output an m-subset. ... an algorithm is \delta-PAC if it stops after \tau rounds, and outputs a set A_\tau that satisfies P(A_\tau \neq A^*) \le \delta.

settings.name_in_paper: Best pair identification with bandit feedback (m=2) (lower bound)
unmapped: Each round the learner pulls an arm pair and observes a sample from the corresponding bivariate marginal of a zero-mean Gaussian K-vector with unknown covariance
Objective: identify the pair minimizing the MSE psi({i,j}) (correlation-based)
settings.definition_quote: We consider a class of algorithms that are $\delta$-PAC for the best pair identification problem with a bandit feedback model, where an algorithm chooses to pull an arm pair and observe a sample from the underlying bivariate distribution in each round.

symbols.Delta_sub: smallest MSE gap among m-subsets, min_A psi(A) - psi(A*)

conditions: Assumption 1: 0 < l <= sigma_i^2 <= 1 for all i
Assumption 2 holds for every m-subset A: max(||Sigma_AA||,||Sigma_A'A'||) <= M_0 and ||Sigma_AA^{-1}|| <= 1/M_1
tuning: confidence width alpha_t as in eq. (alphat_appendix) with confidence delta

source.label: thm:se
source.quote: Assume \ref{ass:variance} and \ref{ass:eigenvalue} for every $A \in \A$. The successive elimination algorithm is $(0, \delta)$-PAC for any $\delta \in (0,1)$, and w.p. at least $1 - \delta$, it's sample complexity is bounded by $\mathcal{O} \left( \frac{1}{\Delta_{\textrm{min}}} \log \left(\frac{\binom{K}{m} \log \left(\Delta^{-1}\right)}{\delta}\right)\right)$, where $\Delta = \min_{A \in \A} \Delta(A)$ denotes the smallest gap.

results.notes: Sample complexity counts the number of K-vector samples (rounds). The algorithm is also delta-PAC. The 1/Delta (not 1/Delta^2) dependence is as stated by the paper. Delta_min and Delta in the statement refer to the same smallest subset gap.

symbols.Delta_sub: smallest MSE gap among arm pairs on the instance governed by Sigma

conditions: there exists an instance (covariance matrix Sigma) for which the bound holds (minimax-type)
sample complexity counts total pair pulls sum_{(i,j)} E[N_ij(tau_delta)]

source.label: thm:lb
source.quote: If the number of arms $K > 7$, then for any $\delta$-PAC algorithm, there exists a bandit problem instance governed by a covariance matrix $\Sigma$ such that the sample complexity $\E_{\Sigma}[\tau_{\delta}]$ of this algorithm satisfies $\E_{\Sigma}[\tau_{\delta}] \geq \frac{K^{2}\log (\frac{1}{2.4 \delta})}{\Delta}.$ where $\Delta$ denotes the smallest gap on the problem instance governed by $\Sigma$.

results.notes: Lower bound for m=2 (best pair) where each round observes one pair's bivariate sample; feedback model differs from the upper bound setting (full K-vector per round).
